### 1. Initial Position and Orientation
- **Solid:** Triangular prism (Base side = $50\text{ mm}$, Axis length = $50\text{ mm}$). Rest on one of its rectangular faces on the H.P.
- **Axis condition:** Axis is initially parallel to both H.P. and V.P.
- **Secondary condition:** Axis is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the V.P. while resting on H.P.

### 2. Drawing Steps
1. **Front View (Stage 1):** Draw an equilateral triangle of side $50\text{ mm}$ resting on one of its sides above or below the $XY$ line (representing the rectangular face resting on HP).
2. **Top View (Stage 1):** Project projectors downwards to draw the rectangular top view of length $50\text{ mm}$.
3. **Secondary Top View (Stage 2):** Tilt the top view such that the axis makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the $XY$ line (representing V.P.).
4. **Secondary Front View:** Project points upwards from the tilted top view and across from the initial front view to obtain the final front view.

### 3. Sectional Top View
1. Locate a horizontal cutting plane parallel to the HP at a distance of $5\text{ mm}$ from the axis in the front view.
2. Project the intersection points of the cutting plane down to the top view.
3. Hatch the cut region using thin 45-degree section lines to obtain the **sectional top view**.
proTip: Hatching lines in sectional views must be drawn uniformly spaced at an angle of 45 degrees to the reference axis.
